Every level, change, sensitivity, channel preference and committee view here is invented. The issuers are real TSX names used only as labels; contacts are ROLES, never invented people at real companies. Macro direction and per-client EBITDA sensitivities were reviewed by a second model (oil supply shock, risk-off): gas moves less than oil; the WCS-WTI differential widens to -17.2; a wider differential moves Gibson's differential hedge toward Gibson, so the Bank's pre-settlement exposure FALLS.
title: Overnight oil supply shock
headline: OPEC+ surprise supply increase: WTI -14.2% overnight, WCS-WTI differential wider by US$4.1, energy credit spreads +62 bp.
alert: Crude fell 14.2% overnight on an unexpected OPEC+ supply increase. Energy credit is repricing and the WCS discount has widened.

CLI-1001.driver: Fee-based infrastructure cushions the hit; crude marketing margin and the Chauvin volumes are exposed to the wider WCS differential.

response.detail: Accepted the Teams video call at 10:30 ET.

CLI-1002.driver: NGL margins and producer activity soften; the fee-for-service base is resilient.

CLI-1003.driver: Light-oil producer: realised prices fall with WTI; the hedge book covers only part of the next 12 months.

CLI-1004.driver: Activity-linked energy-services volumes soften; waste and industrial services are steadier.

CLI-1005.driver: Lower diesel and input costs and USD revenue translation help modestly.

CLI-1006.driver: Energy tubular product demand and industrial sentiment weaken; CAD weakness partly offsets on USD-priced sales.

CLI-1007.driver: Lower energy, freight and input costs offset demand worries.

response.detail: Accepted the Teams video call at 14:00 ET.

CLI-1008.driver: Broadly neutral near term: mixed FX and input-cost effects.

CLI-1009.driver: Fuel and freight relief is offset by a weaker CAD on imported merchandise.

CLI-1010.driver: Propane distribution margins are modestly lower; volumes remain weather-driven.

positions.view: Treat the move as supply-driven, not a demand shock. Base case is a partial retracement over two quarters; do not anchor client conversations on spot.
Expect energy high-yield spreads to stay wide near term; investment-grade midstream remains resilient. No change to midstream appetite.

No new term exposure to producers in the Tight or Breach band without a CP-005 pro-forma at a 15% EBITDA stress. Energy sector envelope is Amber: route new requests through Portfolio Management (CP-002).
Offer hedge-programme reviews to producers, subject to CP-010 appropriateness and pre-settlement capacity. No solicitation on restricted names.
Raise covenant conversations early and attach them to any facility discussion now, not after the next compliance certificate.

approved_framing: Today's move looks supply-driven; our committee's base case is a partial retracement over the next two quarters.
We are not changing our support for well-structured midstream and infrastructure credits.
Any change to facility size or terms is subject to our internal approval; we will come back with something firm.
If it would help, we can review your hedge programme with you - any recommendation follows our appropriateness process.
needs_disclaimer: Any view on commodity prices or spreads (forward-looking; not a forecast or advice).
Any illustration of covenant sensitivity (based on your reported figures; illustrative only).
needs_approval: Any indicative facility size, hold or pricing (CP-003).
Any specific hedge structure or notional (CP-010, and CP-008 where a restriction applies).
never_say: Our internal risk rating, single-name limit or its utilisation (CP-014).
Our sector capacity position or that it constrains us (CP-002).
Anything touching a restricted subject, or that a wall-crossing exists (CP-008).

severity.note: Deterministic 0-100. Weights reviewed by a second model; the derivative factor is replaced by shock magnitude (only one client carries derivatives) and events include live transactions. Threshold 41 flags five of ten, as the reviewer suggested.
